discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed - all 13 matview histogram gates in framework/logstore/rdb.go now require `bucketSizeSeconds%3600 == 0` in addition to `>= 3600`, so non-hour-aligned bucket sizes (e.g. 5400) fall back to the raw-table path with exact timestamp predicates. See updated code.
Hey, what's the purpose for changing this?

reasoning_details get grouped by index downstream, the streaming accumulator does it and OpenRouter style clients do the same. These deltas hardcoded index 0, which was fine while thinking was the only reasoning emitter, but a redacted block in the same stream would now share index 0 with the visible thinking. The two get merged into a single detail typed reasoning.text that also carries data, and since request conversion only turns reasoning.encrypted details back into redacted_thinking blocks, the payload would be dropped again on replay. Per block indices keep the entries separate. Single reasoning block streams still emit index 0 like before, and TestToBifrostChatCompletionStream_MixedReasoningBlocksKeepDistinctIndices pins the mixed case.

Acknowledged. Gemini `Segment` indices are byte offsets while OpenAI `url_citation` expects character offsets, so spans skew for multi-byte UTF-8 content. This is a pre-existing limitation shared with the Responses path (`emitAnnotationsFromGroundingSupports` in `responses.go` passes the same byte offsets through) and is already documented in the helper doc comment (lines 616-618). Fixing it only here would diverge from the Responses path; a consistent rune-offset conversion across both paths is better as a dedicated follow-up. For ASCII content the indices are identical.

Fixed in 94e6d6e65. Added a `deepCopyChatAnnotations` helper that clones the `URLCitation.URL`, `Sources` and `Type` pointer fields per annotation, matching the existing `ReasoningDetails` deep-copy pattern. It is used in both `deepCopyChatStreamDelta` and the `buildCompleteMessageFromChatStreamChunks` accumulator, so the deep-copy ownership boundary is preserved.

discussion_comments.comment_body: This is intentional. Key-order preservation is the point of this change: providers like OpenAI follow the literal key order of the structured-output schema, so decoding into plain Go maps (re-marshaled with sorted keys) degrades output quality. The JSON wire format is unchanged; only Go struct construction changes. Callers can migrate with `schemas.OrderedMapFromMap(...)` (sorted, deterministic) or `schemas.NewOrderedMapFromPairs(...)` (explicit order), mirroring the existing `ToolFunctionParameters` design. The source-compat break is documented in core/changelog.md.
